proofUses.reason: Largest-component expectation. General and critical-reference hypotheses are separated in the article.
Shared-boundary variance. General and critical-reference hypotheses are separated in the article.
Truncated susceptibility and singleton correction. General and critical-reference hypotheses are separated in the article.

Supercritical large-cluster density. General and critical-reference hypotheses are separated in the article.
Concentration and relative largest-component upper bound. General and critical-reference hypotheses are separated in the article.

Sum exact conditional exploration means, bound the active queue within each component by the martingale maximum and drift, and apply the L2 maximal inequality. The restart subtraction and discrete-time quadratic correction are retained.

A long positive excursion gives the giant. Condition only on the completion stopping history for the independent undiscovered remainder. For the sharper remaining ranks, condition explicitly on the selected giant and then remove the complement size condition using a uniform subcritical tail bound.

Supercritical Poisson exploration separates survival mass from the finite Borel tail. Its survival probability is asymptotic to two epsilon; a cutoff between epsilon^(-2) and epsilon N gives the matching expectation upper bound and mean absolute convergence.
Finite edge Menger gives linearly many disjoint paths; the total edge count makes at least half short. Their independent sprinkled openings give an exponential failure bound.

Condition on the initial configuration and union-bound only over partitions of its large components. A deterministic weight partition then puts all but delta N of their vertices in one final component.

At each fixed cutoff, local tree convergence identifies the mean large-cluster mass and bounded dependence gives concentration. Sprinkle from a smaller fixed parameter, then take the cutoff and parameter limits in order; compare total large-cluster mass for uniqueness.

A bond flip changes at most two small components worth of cutoff indicators; locally weighted terms add only a bounded host neighbourhood. Apply the conditional centered-Bernoulli exponential-moment bound to the edge-exposure martingale.

Replace fixed-cutoff variance estimates by exponential bounds, retaining the conditional sprinkling estimate. Fix all cutoffs and the smaller parameter before the graph-size limit; compare large-cluster mass for the second component.

Local convergence identifies the weighted cutoff expectation. Once the largest component exceeds the cutoff, the difference from its weighted mass is bounded by Z_M minus L1; both bounds concentrate exponentially.

Condition the tree root on its open degree and use independent descendant extinction. Sum the degree profile for edges, subtract vertices for excess, and expand the nontrivial fixed point only after the graph-size limit.
Count connected blocks by canonical depth-first walks, sum over root sets and size compositions, and union-bound the probability that at least half a boundary is reserved blue.

Trim a minimum red cut to components meeting its terminal union; the smaller side is thick in the original host. Its red cut supplies short edge-disjoint paths, and the large-component partition bound gives red-only coalescence.

Use local two-sided deletion clusters for the upper bound. Blue first-round edges with two large red clusters become cycle edges after red-only coalescence. Correct the red parameter to (1-theta)p0 and use binomial blue sampling conditional only on the full uncoloured configuration. Compare counts for the local approximation, other cores and bridges.

The limiting selected-edge degree on the regular tree is the number of surviving branches when that number is at least two. Local concentration and the edge symmetric-difference bound transfer this profile to the giant core; binomial identities give vertices, edges and excess.

Choose the deletion witness after fixing the entire configuration, then independently thin. Erasing the incident open edges has a conditional lower probability bound; isolated deleted vertices explain the t>=1 hypothesis.

Compare with a slightly smaller fixed parameter and absorb the exponential erasure cost. The second-largest bound puts the surviving large component inside the original giant; retain the quantifier over all small deletion sets.
Stop depth-first search when exactly ceil(m/3) vertices are finished. Its stack is a path, separates finished from unseen vertices, and leaves both sides of order at most 2m/3.
List successive intersections of the short connector with the long path. One jump in path index is large, and the intervening connector segment is internally disjoint from the path.

Find a long first-round path, sprinkle a bounded-length connection between its outer thirds, and use the intersection lemma to obtain a long cycle. The second-largest bound locates it in the final giant; cycles survive core pruning.
Solve the exact exploration recursion; dyadic martingale maximal estimates control the restart count and last early zero. The existing long excursion identifies the giant.
Bound the conditional binomial variance error in mean and the third absolute moments; telescope conditional characteristic functions and remove deterministic weights in L2.

Localize the giant completion at the fluctuation scale, control weighted martingale oscillations on deterministic intervals, linearize the exact drift and replace its root by the survival-probability center.
Expand the positive survival root to second order and compare its deterministic bias with the Gaussian scale.
Bound conditional centered-binomial exponential moments, stop the resulting nonnegative supermartingale at a crossing and optimize its parameter.
A long component forces a large martingale increment against finite-population depletion. Group start times in deterministic blocks and sum the resulting quadratic block exponents.
Upgrade the deterministic parabolic approximation to exponential probability, locate its long excursion and apply the subcritical tail only conditional on the stopped history.
Control all leading-scale moments of the giant, retain the exact cutoff conditioning of its complement, and bound the exceptional contribution using Holder rather than the ambient vertex count.
Use the exact Poisson dual identity and differentiate the rate near its subcritical dual; the quotient m/c_m cancels exactly in the logarithmic centering.
Condition on the giant set within a slowly growing Gaussian-size interval. Uniform subcritical interval-count limits and negligible cutoff conditioning factor from the giant-size event.
Express each ordered-size event as inequalities for exceedance counts; the exponential arrival representation identifies the joint rank vector and the tree property.
Expand the exact supercritical rate and retain its bias times the logarithmic centering; use tightness for the diverging-shift case.
Apply a weighted exponential maximal bound on dyadic time intervals to the drifted minimum and late zeros of the exploration.
Control completion-time fluctuations by the martingale maximum and early errors on the good trajectory; bound every exceptional-event moment using the global largest-component tail.
Transfer uniform centered subcritical moments through the cutoff-conditioned complement, with random rate and centering errors controlled in moments; apply uniform integrability to the joint limit.
Compute logarithmic gamma covariances by the beta-gamma factorization and differentiate the gamma product; the Gaussian/extreme covariance vanishes by independence.
Coordinate-exposure exponential moments bound distances to a large set; greedy exclusion of radius-ell neighbourhoods packs vertex-disjoint paths.
A balanced partition of final component masses is a union of first-round components; count those partitions and use independent sprinkled paths.
Verify the cube reference assumptions, concentrate first-round mass and compare the path-success exponent N^(1-o(1)) with at most exp(O(N^(5/6))) partitions.
Mean-square concentration of large-cluster mass bounds the giant second moment and total component squares; transitivity yields susceptibility and negligible remainder.
